title: Routing Bridge — Customer Brief and Action Lanes (2029-10-03)
content:
TL;DR
On 2029-10-02 22:10 UTC we observed an increase in routed requests to a new model variant in our EU region due to an automated policy misclassification in the routing bridge. A subset of requests experienced higher-than-normal latency and a small percentage returned truncated structured outputs. No customer data was lost. We opened this note to: (1) give a concise status update for impacted tenants, (2) outline immediate action lanes customers can take, and (3) summarize technical root cause and remediation steps.

Who this is for
- Primary: engineering/product leads at tenants using EU inference endpoints, streaming or structured output features.
- Secondary: platform and SRE points of contact for enterprise accounts.

Impact summary (customer-facing)
- Window: 2029-10-02 22:10 UTC — 2029-10-03 00:45 UTC (partial recovery started 22:40 UTC; final mitigations completed 00:45 UTC).
- Symptoms: increased median latency in EU region (200ms -> 650ms), intermittent truncated structured outputs for ~0.8% of inference calls, and a higher-than-expected tail latency for streaming sessions.
- Scope: ~3.2% of active tenants experienced measurable degradation; of those, ~15 tenants had developer-visible truncated JSON outputs.
- Data integrity: No evidence of data corruption or token loss. Requests were processed; truncations were response-length related.

What we did (operator summary)
1) Identified signal: automated routing telemetry flagged a rise in usage of a model variant labeled "v2-bridge"; latency and kv-cache miss rates spiked.
2) Immediate mitigation (22:40 UTC): temporarily disabled the routing bridge policy that auto-promotes v2-bridge in EU. Traffic reverted to pinned model variants for affected tenants.
3) Recovery (23:10 UTC): restarted the regional routing controller with adjusted promotion thresholds, introduced a temporary per-tenant circuit break for bursty traffic.
4) Final rollback (00:45 UTC): removed the errant promotion rule and deployed a canary of a safer routing policy; monitoring confirmed tail latency returned to baseline.

Root cause (summary for customers)
- The routing bridge contains heuristics to promote lower-cost model variants when latency profiles and capacity permit. A recent change in promotion logic (runtime PR #1897) incorrectly treated short-burst patterns as sustained capacity, which allowed v2-bridge to be promoted prematurely. v2-bridge has slightly different output chunking behavior; under unexpected burst conditions this amplified streaming tail latency and produced truncated structured outputs for long responses.

Current status (as of 2029-10-03 10:00 UTC)
- Host service: fully recovered in EU; global routing operating normally.
- Customer impact: customers who experienced truncation were offered immediate replay options and can request evidence bundles (see below).
- Safeguards added: promotion thresholds hardened, promotion events now require two-signal confirmation and a gradual ramp.

Customer action lanes (pick one; short instructions)
1) Safe Mode (recommended for short term stability): Pin to an explicit model version in the tenant config. Steps: Console > Models > Pin > select stable model (e.g., "rwd-gpt-stable-3.1"). No code change needed.
2) Opt-in Replay (for verifying outputs): If you observed truncated responses, request a replay of the affected time range. We provide a replay package containing original request timestamps and candidate replays with the stable model applied. To request: open a support ticket with subject "Routing Bridge Replay Request" and include sample request IDs or time range.
3) Tighten structured-output length guard (recommended for streaming): Add a client-side guard to trim generation max_tokens or add incremental flush boundaries. See snippet in linked artifacts (Confluence: structured-output-guard).

Verification checklist customers can run
- Confirm latency baseline: sample steady-state /v1/generate p95 < 300ms from EU region.
- Validate structured output: run 10 representative prompts that previously produced truncated outputs and compare to expected parseable JSON.
- If you have automatic rollbacks with our SDK, ensure that your model-pin policy catches promotion events (we added a new webhook event type: routing.promotion).

Evidence and replay packages
- We can provide a per-tenant evidence bundle containing: request timestamps, request IDs, truncated responses, and operator timeline. To request, reply to your account rep or open a ticket with ticket key prefix RB-EVID- and provide consent for package delivery.

FAQ (short)
Q: Will this happen again?
A: We added confirmation signals and ramping to promotion logic; risk reduced substantially. We also backfilled telemetry to catch similar patterns.

Q: Were any private deployments affected?
A: No, private deployments with their control-plane disabled were not affected; only hosted/dedicated EU control plane instances running the problematic promotion rule were impacted.

Q: Do I need to change my prompts or model configs?
A: Not required. If you rely on long structured outputs, consider pinning until your team verifies results with the new policy.

Next steps (what Redwood is doing)
- Short-term (24–72h): additional telemetry filters and end-to-end regression tests for output chunking under bursty conditions; post-deployment canary for routing promoter.
- Mid-term (2–4 weeks): make promotion ramp parameters tenant-configurable and add an opt-out flag for automatic promotions.
- Postmortem: detailed internal RCA and timeline will be published in Confluence (linked artifact), and we will notify tenants when the public postmortem is available.

Contact & support
- Immediate help: open a priority ticket via your support portal and reference "Routing Bridge".
- For partners/enterprise: contact your solutions engineer or email enterprise-support@redwood.ai.
- Slack ops channel: #cust-ops (monitoring thread pinned).

Notes to self / draft items (work-in-progress)
- Decide whether to offer credit for impacted tenants: discuss with finance/legal.
- Collate list of exact tenant IDs and attach to evidence bundles (SRE to prepare).
- Validate sample size used for the 3.2% tenant impact calculation and confirm with analytics.

Appendix: short timeline (operator times UTC)
- 2029-10-02 22:10: first signal (routing telemetry)
- 22:18: engineers triaged; root cause suspected in promotion logic
- 22:40: temporary disable of promotion policy (partial recovery)
- 23:10: routing controller restart + circuit breaker applied
- 00:45: final rollback of promotion rule; canary deployed
- 2029-10-03 02:00: monitoring confirms p95/p99 latency returned to baseline

End of brief — feedback welcome. This is a working draft meant for distribution to impacted engineering contacts and enterprise stakeholders; please send edits to Asha Patel (owner) or add inline comments in this doc.
